title: 孩子们的盗版指南
author: Hacker News
content:
24 Jul 2026

Hey kids! Have you heard of piracy but don’t know how to do it cos you grew up while streaming worked okay? Well this is the guide for you!

DISCLAIMER: It is only my intent that the advice offered here be used to download media that is in the public domain. While it’s true that the advice here could be employed to download recent movies and TV shows that are under copyright, and that that is its primary application, it’s cerrrtainnnly not my intention that you use it for such purposes. You wouldn’t want to deprive a media megacorp CEO of his second yacht would you?!?!

ALSO KIND OF A DISCLAIMER I GUESS: I’ll be describing how to do this on a personal computer of some sort (that includes laptops (that includes your macintosh-books and so on)). You can probably do it on the portable telephones you all seem to love so much, but I have no idea how because I am old.

What is torrenting?

Torrenting is how we used to get movies and TV shows and games back before streaming and Steam were things and before we realised the error of our ways and bucked our ideas up.

I’m going to be nutshelling this pretty hard, describing things very broadly, so don’t come “Well actually…”ing me about details, I don’t care. And if you’re not interested in how it all works, just skip down to the numbered instructions.

Movies and TV shows, in digital form, are just files. And you want to download those files to your computer where you can do what you like with them. Watch them whenever you want, copy them to other devices, back them up, take clips and edit them together to some horrible pop music and upload that to TikTok. Whatever you like.

Torrenting lets you do that. The downloading part. A torrent is a description of how to download those files from other people who have them. When you are torrenting something, you are simultaneously downloading it from other people who have it and uploading it to other people who want it. The uploading and downloading stop when you close the client or remove that particular torrent from the client.

Popular things, which lots of people are sharing, will download more quickly (often as fast as your internet can go) than niche things. But pretty much anything should download eventually if you just leave the torrent client running.

You generally have to download something completely before you can watch it, this isn’t streaming. If it’s a TV show, though, you can choose to only download particular episodes, or prioritise particular episodes so they download first and you can watch them while the next one downloads.

Your internet service provider (ISP) may be able to tell when you’re torrenting, and may care. The worst that’s likely to happen in this instance is that they’ll send you a letter telling you to stop. If this is a concern for you, only torrent while using a VPN, this will mask your torrenting from your ISP.

1. Get a torrent client

A torrent client is a program (‘app’) that lets you download torrents. You’ll need one of those. There are many many torrent clients and, once you’re up and running, feel free to try other ones out. For now I’ll just recommend basic ones that work well.

If you’re on Windows, download qBittorrent.

If you’re on MacOS or Linux, download Transmission.

Install the one you downloaded.

Pop it open and have a look at the interface if you like. Now we need to get a torrent file.

2. Choose a tracker

Trackers are websites that list and allow you to search for torrents. There are many of these. Some are member-only, some are public, some are specialised to a particular kind of media, some are general. We’ll start with a general, public one.

Go to https://1337x.to/ and search for the movie, TV show or whatever you want to download.

You’ll probably see multiple options. If it’s a TV show or movie you’re searching for, the filename on the left will contain information such as the resolution (720, 1080, 4k and so on), the video encoder used such as ‘x264’, ‘x265’ and others, don’t worry about that for now. Audio format and encoder used and, again, don’t worry about that for now. And finally file format such as ‘mkv’, ‘mp4’ and so on, and again, don’t worry. You’ll probably mostly care about resolution - the larger the resolution, the larger the file size (and so the longer it’ll take to download, generally speaking).

Choose something appropriate - probably something 720 or 1080 for now. Then have a look at the other columns.

  • se is the number of seeders - that is people actively uploading the file(s).
  • le is the number of leechers - that is people downloading the file(s).
  • date is when the torrent was created.
  • size is how big the files are to download.
  • uploader is the username of the person who uploaded the torrent to this tracker.

Generally you’ll want to choose something with a lot of seeders, i.e. where the se number is higher. More seeders means faster downloads.

Some tips:

If you’re looking for a single episode, stick the season and episode number into the search in the form ‘S01E01’. Changing the numbers appropriately, of course.

If you want a particular season, stick ‘S01’ and ‘complete’ into the search. Again, changing the number appropriately.

If you’re after a movie and there are multiple movies with that name, add the year of release to your search terms.

3. Tell your torrent client to download the torrent

Pick one and click on the filename of the one you’ve chosen. That will take you to a page about that particular torrent. Have a look at all that info if you want, and then, when you’re ready, either:

Click on the green “magnet download” button in the upper right. At which point, if your operating system has created the right associations, your torrent client should pop up and ask if you want to download that torrent. Click on Open/Download/whatever.

Or: Right-click that green “magnet download” button and ‘copy link’ or ‘copy link address’. Then open your torrent client, at which point it may offer to download the torrent if it recognises that you’ve copied the link, in which case click on Open/Download/whatever. If not:

On Transmission, click on ‘file’ in Transmission’s program menu, and click ‘Open URL’. Paste the torrent link into the ‘Source:’ box and then click the ‘Open’ button down at the bottom of that window.

On qBittorent, click on the ‘add torrent link’ button, which is the first button on the left under the file menu. It’s probably blue and looks like two revolving arrows with a blob in the middle. Paste the link into the box that pops up, again it may already be there, and then click the ‘Download’ button near the bottom of that window.

And that’s it, the torrent is added to the client and the files will start downloading. It may start slow but it’ll generally pick up speed over time as it discovers more clients to download from.

By default, the files will download to your ‘Downloads’ folder. You can change this location (and lots of other things) in the torrent client’s settings if you like.

4. Watch!

Wait for the files to download. Your torrent client will present loads of information such as how many people you’re downloading from, the speed of the download, an ETA for completion and so on.

Once the files are downloaded (your torrent client will make it clear when they’re complete), go to your Downloads folder, find the files (they’ll likely be in a folder named similarly to the file you chose on the tracker) and just double click the media files (‘.mp4’, ‘.mkv’, ‘.m4v’ and so on). They should open in your default media player.

If you don’t have a good media player, VLC is a decent option. You can download it here.

5. Remove the torrent from the client

Once you’re done downloading, leave the torrent uploading to other people (‘seeding’) for a while, cos that’s a nice thing to do and is how this whole thing works. Then, when you’re happy that you’ve done your bit, remove the torrent from the client (just right click the torrent and click ‘remove’). This won’t remove the files you downloaded, just the torrent from the client.

oneSentenceSummary: 一份幽默的、逐步的指南，面向新手，教他们如何使用 BitTorrent 客户端下载电影和电视剧。
summary: 文章采用活泼的语气，向成长于流媒体时代的一代人介绍了种子下载的基础。它解释了什么是种子，qBittorrent 和 Transmission 等客户端如何工作，并逐步讲解完整流程：选择公共追踪器（1337x），选择种子数较多的种子，添加磁力链接，下载，最后观看媒体。指南还介绍了做种礼仪，并简要提到使用 VPN 以避免收到 ISP 警告。内容实用、面向新手，且刻意不深入技术细节。

mainPoints.point: 种子下载允许你通过同时上传和下载从其他用户那里获取文件。
mainPoints.explanation: 这是一种与流媒体不同的点对点方式。热门种子下载速度更快，因为更多人在做种。

mainPoints.point: 指南详细说明了完整的工作流程：安装客户端，寻找追踪器，选择种子数较多的种子，添加磁力链接，然后等待下载。
mainPoints.explanation: 它推荐在 Windows 使用 qBittorrent，在 macOS/Linux 使用 Transmission，并以 1337x 作为公共追踪器的示例。

mainPoints.point: 下载后，鼓励用户在移除种子之前先做种（上传）以帮助他人。
mainPoints.explanation: 做种被呈现为良好礼仪，并且对系统正常运作至关重要。移除种子不会影响已下载文件的完整性。

keyQuotes: 你不会想剥夺媒体巨头 CEO 的第二艘游艇，对吧？？？
种子下载是我们在流媒体和 Steam 尚未普及之前获取电影、电视剧和游戏的方式，在那时我们才意识到自己的做法有误，并改变了想法。
